dataset: Test score concordance tables for the Competitiveness Index (lib/stand/rules.ts): English tests on the IELTS scale, GMAT on the Focus Edition scale
notes: A TOEFL iBT or PTE Academic score is put on the IELTS Academic band scale with these tables, and so is the programme's own minimum for that test; the index then measures the margin in IELTS bands.

TOEFL iBT moved to a 1-6 scale on 21 January 2026. Scores on the 0-120 scale (tests before that date, and the comparable score on every report for two years) are first read on the 1-6 scale with ETS's own comparison, then on IELTS.
Each IELTS band's row is the lowest score on the other test ETS or Pearson lists for that band. A score is read as the highest band whose row it reaches.

A GMAT score is read on the GMAT Focus Edition scale (205-805), and so is the programme's own GMAT figure. A 10th Edition (classic, 200-800) score reads as the middle of the Focus Edition scores GMAC's table pairs it with (700: 645 and 655, so 650). Which edition a score is goes by its last digit: 5 Focus Edition, any other 10th Edition (Kaplan 360++'s rule).

source.title: TOEFL iBT Score Scale 1 to 6: CEFR & IELTS Comparison
source.quote: The tables are based on a score concordance study between the previous TOEFL iBT and IELTS, and vertical linking research which connected the reading and listening scores from the 0-30 section score scale to an earlier version of the 1-6 score scale.

source.title: PTE Academic scoring: PTE Academic and IELTS Academic
source.quote: our concordance with IELTS has been updated based on research published in July 2025

source.title: GMAT Score Concordance Table: Total Score Sorted by Percentile Ranking
source.quote: Use this table to compare GMAT™ Exam (10th Edition) Total Scores and GMAT Exam (Focus Edition) Total Scores and to understand corresponding percentile values.
source.dataPeriod: The percentile values in this document are based on the data period between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2026.

gmat.rowsNote: Each row as GMAC prints it, in its order: [10th Edition total, Focus Edition total, percentile].
